findings.message: The new clue "blink-code" (story.r9.json lines 66-68: "When Ivy called out, the little box blinked and thudded twice, slow and quick. Something was listening.") describes the box's blink-and-thud as a response to Ivy calling out. But the passage text that precedes the choice already narrates the same thud unconditionally for both branches (line 381: "Then it gave a soft thud, twice, like a secret code."), before either choice is picked. So the clue's own causal claim ("when Ivy called out") contradicts the passage, which shows the thud happening on its own, not as a reaction to the call-out choice. Reword the clue text (or move the thud into the call-out branch only) so the clue does not assert a cause-and-effect that the passage itself does not show.

Both new collectibles added in this revision (item "chalk-note", lines 54-56; clue "blink-code", lines 66-68) are picked up via engine-trace's "call-out" and nib-ask's "promise-nib" and then never referenced again anywhere in the draft (confirmed by searching the full r9 draft for "chalk-note" and "blink-code": each appears only in its item/clue definition and its one addItems/addClues effect). This differs from the story's existing pattern, where every other item/clue (hook-pole, late-log) is both collectible and later paid off - gating the open-careful locked choice and being named again in climax-careful's text ("Bo held the hook-pole. Ivy read the last note aloud."). Leaving the two new collectibles with no later narrative or mechanical payoff is not a blocker (they do not gate anything, so they cannot cause a soft-lock or change ending reachability - confirmed by graph.r9.json, 5/5 endings reachable, and by grep showing no `requires` block anywhere references either id), but it is a content-integrity gap worth closing before the next pass: either reference the chalk note or the blinking code again later (an ending line, or a beat at threshold/climax-careful), or rewrite the two choice labels so they read as pure atmosphere rather than a kept "promise"/discovered "code" that the story then drops. This is the same root cause on both passages: nib-ask's unconditional line 435 ("Nib snapped off a small chalk note and held it out, like a gift") happens before the choice, so the nib-ask-on branch silently ignores an already-offered gift with no acknowledgement either way.
